title: Where to stay in Malta: the best areas explained
seo_title: Where to Stay in Malta (2026): Best Areas for Every Type of Trip
meta: Valletta, Sliema, St Julian's, the Three Cities, St Paul's Bay or Rabat? A local guide to the best areas to stay in Malta, who each one suits and how to get around.
tldr: First trip and no car: Valletta or Sliema. Nightlife and restaurants: St Julian's. Authentic and good value: the Three Cities. Beaches and boat trips: St Paul's Bay and the north. Space, terraces and pools: Msida, Pietà and Ta' Xbiex. Countryside and quiet: Rabat near Mdina.

sections.h: Valletta: for history and walking everywhere
p: Valletta is the capital and a UNESCO World Heritage city, small enough to cross on foot in fifteen minutes. You step out onto baroque streets, St John's Co-Cathedral and the Upper Barrakka Gardens, and the main bus terminus at the city gate connects you to the rest of the island.
It suits first-time visitors, couples and anyone who wants to leave the car behind. Homes here are inside historic buildings, so expect stairs and character rather than lifts and big terraces.

sections.h: Sliema: for the seafront and an easy base
p: Sliema runs along a long promenade with rocky swimming spots, cafés and the Tigné Point shopping area. The ferry to Valletta leaves from the Strand and takes about ten minutes, and buses from here reach most of the island.
It is the easiest base for families and for anyone who wants the sea, restaurants and transport at the door.

sections.h: St Julian's: for restaurants and going out
p: St Julian's wraps around Balluta, Spinola and St George's Bay. Spinola Bay is lined with restaurants, St George's Bay has a sandy beach, and the Paceville nightlife district is a few streets away.
Stay in the residential streets around Spinola and Balluta if you want to be close to the action and still sleep well.

sections.h: The Three Cities: for an authentic, local Malta
p: Cospicua (Bormla), Senglea (Isla) and Birgu (Vittoriosa) sit across the Grand Harbour from Valletta. They are older than the capital, still lived in by Maltese families, and far quieter. A ferry crosses to Valletta in minutes.
Prices are lower than in Valletta or Sliema, which makes the Three Cities a smart choice for couples and solo travellers who want character.

sections.h: Msida, Pietà and Ta' Xbiex: for space in the centre
p: These harbour towns sit between Valletta and Sliema, around the yacht marinas. They are where you find penthouses with terraces and private pools for the price of a smaller flat in the capital, with Valletta five minutes away.

sections.h: St Paul's Bay and the north: for beaches and boat trips
p: St Paul's Bay, Bugibba and Qawra form the holiday hub of the north coast. Boat trips to Comino and the Blue Lagoon leave from the bay, and the sandy beaches of Mellieħa and Golden Bay are a short drive away. A car is useful up here.

sections.h: Rabat and Mdina: for a quieter, rural Malta
p: Rabat sits at the gates of Mdina, the walled medieval city in the centre of the island. It is the best base for the Dingli Cliffs, the west coast beaches and slower days away from the coast.

sections.h: What about Gozo?
p: Gozo, Malta's sister island, is greener and slower. The ferry from Ċirkewwa takes about 25 minutes. Many visitors stay on Malta and visit Gozo for a day, or split their trip between the two.

faq: What is the best area to stay in Malta for the first time?
Valletta or Sliema. Both let you explore without a car, have plenty of restaurants and are connected by a ten-minute ferry.
Where should I stay in Malta without a car?
Valletta, Sliema or St Julian's. The bus network and the harbour ferries cover everything you need from these areas.
Which part of Malta has the best beaches?
The north: Mellieħa Bay, Golden Bay and Għajn Tuffieħa have the island's best sandy beaches. Sliema and St Julian's have rocky swimming spots and the small sandy St George's Bay.

title: Valletta or Sliema: where should you stay?
seo_title: Sliema vs Valletta: Which Is the Better Base in Malta?
meta: Sliema vs Valletta: pick Valletta for history and evenings in the old city, Sliema for swimming, shops and the seafront. A local guide to help you choose.
tldr: Pick Valletta if you want history, culture and evenings in a beautiful old city. Pick Sliema if you want to swim, shop and have an easy seafront base. They are ten minutes apart by ferry, so you will see both either way.

Couples, culture lovers, short city breaks
Families, longer stays, beach and city mix

sections.h: Why choose Valletta
p: Valletta is one of the most beautiful small capitals in Europe. Staying inside the walls means early mornings in empty baroque streets, sunset at the Upper Barrakka Gardens and dinner a few steps from your door. Museums, St John's Co-Cathedral and the Grand Harbour are all on foot.
The trade-off is that Valletta homes are in historic buildings: lifts are rare, rooms can be less bright, and there is little outdoor space. Evenings are calmer than in Sliema or St Julian's.

sections.h: Why choose Sliema
p: Sliema is built for easy days by the sea. The promenade runs for kilometres, you can swim from the rocks in summer, and there are cafés, supermarkets and shops on every street. The ferry from the Strand takes you to Valletta in about ten minutes, and you are a short walk from St Julian's.
It is busier and more modern than Valletta, and homes here are more likely to have balconies, sea views and lifts.

sections.h: Our recommendation
p: For a short city break of three or four nights, or if this is your first time, stay in Valletta and take the ferry to Sliema. For a week or more, with children, or if swimming is a priority, stay in Sliema and take the ferry to Valletta. If you want a third option with real local character and lower prices, look at the Three Cities across the harbour.

faq: How far is Valletta from Sliema?
About ten minutes by ferry across Marsamxett Harbour, or 15 to 25 minutes by bus depending on traffic.
Is Sliema or Valletta better for families?
Sliema usually works better for families: more space, lifts, the promenade for walks and swimming spots close by.
Is Valletta noisy at night?
No. Valletta is lively in the evenings around Republic Street and Strait Street but most residential streets are quiet at night.

title: Malta in winter: weather, what to do and where to stay
seo_title: Malta in Winter: Weather, Things to Do and Where to Stay
meta: Is Malta worth visiting in winter? What the weather is really like from November to March, the best things to do, winter events and how to choose a warm, comfortable place to stay.
tldr: Malta is mild in winter, with daytime temperatures usually in the mid to high teens Celsius, quiet streets and lower prices. It is ideal for city breaks, walking and long stays. Pick a home with good heating and plan a few indoor days for rain.

sections.h: What the weather is like
p: From December to February, daytime temperatures usually sit around 15 to 17°C, dropping to around 10°C at night. Most of the year's rain falls between October and January, often in short heavy showers between sunny spells. The sea is too cool for most people to swim, but walking, cycling and sightseeing are far more comfortable than in the summer heat.

sections.h: Why winter is a good time to visit
p: The streets of Valletta, Mdina and the Three Cities are quiet, flights and accommodation cost less, and you see Malta as locals live it. Winter is also popular with remote workers and long-stay guests, who get the best value on monthly rates.

sections.h: Winter events worth planning around
p: December brings Christmas lights and nativity cribs across the island, with Valletta at the centre. The Valletta Baroque Festival fills churches and palaces with concerts in January. Carnival takes over Valletta and Gozo in February, with floats, costumes and street parties.

sections.h: Things to do on a winter trip
p: Walk the coastal paths at Dingli Cliffs and the north, explore the museums and palaces of Valletta, cross to the Three Cities by ferry, spend a day in Mdina and Rabat, and take the ferry to Gozo on a clear day. Some boat tours to Comino run a reduced timetable in winter, so check before you go.

sections.h: Where to stay in winter
p: Maltese stone buildings stay cool, which is perfect in August and less so in January. Choose a home with air conditioning that heats as well as cools, and consider a cosier place over a big open-plan villa. All our homes have heating, several have fireplaces or fire pits, and our local team is on WhatsApp if anything needs attention.
For winter city breaks, Valletta and the Three Cities are the most atmospheric. For longer stays, Sliema and Msida offer the most services within walking distance.

faq: Is Malta warm in winter?
Mild rather than warm. Expect around 15 to 17°C during the day and about 10°C at night, with plenty of sunny days between showers.
Can you swim in Malta in winter?
A few hardy locals do, but the sea is around 15°C in February. Most visitors save swimming for May to November.
Is Malta cheaper in winter?
Yes. Flights and accommodation are usually much cheaper from November to March, apart from the Christmas and New Year period.

title: Long stays in Malta: renting for a month or more
seo_title: Long Stays in Malta: Monthly Rentals and Where to Live
meta: Staying in Malta for a month or more? Where to base yourself, what to look for in a monthly rental, rooms or apartments, and how to get a long-stay rate.
tldr: Malta works well for stays of a month or more, especially from October to May when the weather is mild and prices are lower. Pick a base by how you will spend your days, choose a home with a desk, a washing machine and heating, and ask us for a monthly rate: stays of a month or more get a special rate.

sections.h: Why spend a month in Malta
p: English is an official language, the island is small enough to know well in a few weeks, and the winters are mild with plenty of sunny days. Flights connect Malta with most European cities, so it suits remote workers, people between jobs or homes, and anyone who wants a slower trip than a long weekend allows.

sections.h: Sliema and St Julian's: everything on the doorstep
p: The busiest and most convenient base. Supermarkets, gyms, cafés with WiFi and the seafront promenade are all walkable, and buses and the Valletta ferry leave from the Strand. It costs more than the rest of the island, and summer nights can be lively.

sections.h: Msida, Pietà and Ta' Xbiex: central, calmer and more space
p: Between Valletta and Sliema, around the marina. You get more space and terraces for your money, quieter evenings and quick access to both cities. It is a practical choice for working weeks.

sections.h: The Three Cities: local life and the best value
p: Birgu, Senglea and Bormla face Valletta across the Grand Harbour. Life here is slower and more local, the waterfront is beautiful, and the ferry gets you to Valletta in a few minutes. Our guest house rooms here have private bathrooms and a shared kitchen, and some are offered only for stays of 28 nights or more.

sections.h: What to look for in a long-stay home
p: A proper desk and a good chair if you will work. A washing machine, and ideally a dryer for winter. Heating as well as air conditioning, because Maltese stone houses feel cold from December to February. A full kitchen, since you will cook more than on a holiday. And a local team that answers quickly when something needs fixing.

sections.h: Rooms or a whole apartment
p: A private ensuite room with a shared kitchen is the lowest-cost way to stay a month, and suits solo travellers and couples who are out most of the day. A whole apartment gives you a separate living space and your own kitchen, which matters more the longer you stay or if you work from home.

sections.h: Practical things to sort before you come
p: EU citizens can stay without a visa. Most other visitors can stay up to 90 days in any 180 under the Schengen rules, and Malta also has a residence permit for remote workers, so check the official rules for your passport before you book. Most homes include cleaning between guests only, so for stays of a month or more we agree a cleaning schedule with you.

faq: Do you offer monthly rates?
Yes. Stays of a month or more get a special rate. Send us your dates on WhatsApp or by email and we will quote you directly.
What is the best time of year for a long stay in Malta?
October to May. The weather is mild, prices are lower than in summer and the island is quieter. July and August are hot and busy.
Can I get cleaning during a long stay?
Yes. For stays of a month or more, message us and we will agree a cleaning schedule that suits you.
Which area is best for remote workers?
Sliema and St Julian's if you want cafés, gyms and coworking on foot. Msida, Pietà or Ta' Xbiex if you want more space and quieter days while staying central.

title: Malta for couples: romantic places to stay and things to do
seo_title: Malta for Couples: Romantic Stays and Things to Do
meta: Planning a trip to Malta for two? The most romantic areas to stay, sunset spots, day trips and the homes our guests choose for couples and special occasions.
tldr: For a couple's trip to Malta, stay in Valletta or the Three Cities for history and harbour views, or near Mdina for quiet evenings and countryside sunsets. Spring and autumn are the best months: warm, calm and less crowded. Choose a home with something special, like a private courtyard, a rooftop pool or a soaking tub.

sections.h: The most romantic areas to stay
p: Valletta is the classic choice: honey-coloured streets, harbour views and dinner within walking distance every night. The Three Cities across the harbour feel even more intimate, with a quiet waterfront and the ferry to Valletta at the door. Mdina and Rabat are best for slow days and silent evenings inside the old walled city. Sliema and St Julian's suit couples who want the sea, restaurants and nightlife close by.

sections.h: The Three Cities: harbour views and quiet streets
p: Senglea, Birgu and Bormla are where many locals take visitors they want to impress. Walk to the Gardjola Gardens lookout in Senglea, cross the harbour on a traditional dgħajsa boat, and eat on the Birgu waterfront as the lights of Valletta come on.

sections.h: Mdina and Rabat: slow days and sunsets
p: Mdina is at its most beautiful at night, when the day visitors have gone. Dingli Cliffs, a short drive away, is one of the best sunset spots on the island, and the countryside around Rabat is lovely for walking.

sections.h: Things to do together
p: Watch the sunset from the Upper Barrakka Gardens in Valletta or from Dingli Cliffs. Take a boat to Comino and the Blue Lagoon early in the day before the crowds. Spend a day on Gozo for its quieter beaches and villages. Book a table at Spinola Bay in St Julian's, and wander Mdina after dark.

sections.h: When to go
p: April to June and September to October are ideal: warm enough to swim, but calmer and less crowded than July and August. Winter is mild and quiet, and a good time for city breaks with cosy evenings in.

faq: What is the most romantic area to stay in Malta?
Valletta for the classic city break, the Three Cities for harbour views and a more local feel, and Mdina or Rabat for peace and countryside sunsets.
Is Malta good for a honeymoon or anniversary?
Yes. It is easy to get around, the food and wine are good, and you can mix city days in Valletta with beaches, boat trips and a day on Gozo. Tell us if you are celebrating when you book direct.
What is the best month for a couples trip to Malta?
May, June, September and October offer warm weather and calm seas without the peak summer crowds.
